channel.title: Sunward
channel.description: Only good news. Each morning Sunward reads real newsrooms, keeps the stories where something got better, and says why in one line.

item.title: Land Returned to Native American Ownership 400 Years After the First Thanksgiving
item.description: About 126 acres of Cape Cod salt marsh and forest have been returned to Native American ownership. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: First hippo born at safari park in more than 40 years
item.description: Longleat Safari Park has its first hippo calf in more than 40 years, born through a European breeding programme. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: Viaduct gardens vision on show as group gets access
item.description: A community group in Leamington has access to a disused viaduct and plans five shared garden spaces along it. How you can help: Join a community garden near you, or ask your council about unused land that could become one. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: James Webb discovers a nearly pristine galaxy from 13 billion years ago
item.description: The Webb telescope found a nearly untouched galaxy from 13 billion years ago that may hold traces of the first stars. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: The narwhal’s legendary “unicorn horn” holds a remarkable engineering secret
item.description: X-ray scans show how the narwhal's spiral tusk is built to be both strong and flexible. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists turn one of the world’s hardest-to-recycle plastics into high-performance lubricating oil
item.description: Virginia Tech chemists turned hard-to-recycle PVC into a high-grade ingredient for engine oil. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Making Peace With a Himalayan ‘Ghost’
item.description: Herders in Ladakh are learning to live alongside snow leopards instead of losing livestock to them. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Floating nature islands installed in parks as Glasgow Games legacy
item.description: Floating planted islands in five Glasgow parks will give wildlife a home and help clean the water. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: Family Is Thankful Their Baby, Given Weeks to Live on Christmas Eve, Now Brain Cancer-Free
item.description: A baby given weeks to live is now free of an aggressive brain cancer after joining a hospital's new treatment study. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Texans Work for Free on Farms That Aren’t Theirs to Send Others’ Kids to College
item.description: Texans farm borrowed land for free each year and turn the harvest into college money for local students. How you can help: Offer a few hours of your skills to a local scholarship or community fund. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: The Portlanders Turning Rescued Food Into Restaurant-Quality Meals
item.description: Portland chefs turn rescued surplus food into restaurant-quality meals for people who need them. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Volunteer with a local food rescue group that collects surplus from shops. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Scientists discover mysterious lakes more than a mile beneath the Red Sea
item.description: Rare brine lakes found deep under the Red Sea may hold clues to Earth's early oceans. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Roman Glass Among the Silk Road Treasures Unearthed in Nomadic Noble’s Tomb
item.description: A nomadic noble's tomb in Mongolia held Roman glass, showing how far Silk Road trade reached. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: ‘Autos for Love’ Owners Delight in Giving Away Cars to Needy Neighbors
item.description: A Texas repair shop refurbishes donated cars and hands the keys to neighbours who need a way to get around. How you can help: Donate a car you no longer need to a charity that refurbishes vehicles for families. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: A space telescope hunting for dark matter just discovered something unexpected
item.description: The Euclid telescope, built to map dark matter, spotted its first new comet. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Physicists trap antimatter in a breakthrough that could explain why the universe exists
item.description: Physicists held a single positron near absolute zero, a step toward learning why matter won out. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Miki Kawamura: a 19-year-old’s peace network brings ice cream to a Nobel summit
item.description: A 19-year-old's peace network brought young people and a shared treat to a Nobel peace summit. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Major Success Sees Viral Infections Fall 68% in Brazil After Releasing Wolbachia-Infected Mosquitoes
item.description: Releasing Wolbachia mosquitoes in Brazil cut mosquito-borne viral infections in schoolchildren by 68 percent. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Retired Teacher Turns Retired Musical Instruments into Bird Feeders (LOOK)
item.description: A retired teacher in Canada turns scrapped guitars and violins into free bird feeders. How you can help: Put out a bird feeder this winter and clean it every couple of weeks. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: A Childhood Promise Mobilizes ‘Thanksgiving Heroes,’ Serving Thousands Nationwide This Holiday
item.description: A boy's promise to his mother grew into Thanksgiving Heroes, which will feed 3,600 Utah families this year. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Volunteer a shift at your local food bank during the holidays. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Charity Swaps Tuition Fees for Coconuts So Every Islander Can Afford School
item.description: A school in Micronesia accepts coconuts in place of tuition so every island family can afford classes. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: 2,200-year-old Roman shipwreck reveals an ingenious waterproofing trick
item.description: A 2,200-year-old Roman shipwreck shows sailors sealed hulls with pine tar and beeswax. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Why a Viagra-like blood flow drug may open a new front against Alzheimer’s
item.description: A daily tablet slowed memory decline by 31 percent over a year in people with early Alzheimer's. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: 33 Kids Wrote Letters to a Wounded Veteran. 60 Years Later, His Son Is Searching to Thank Each One
item.description: A veteran's son is tracking down 33 schoolchildren whose 1967 letters lifted his wounded father, to thank each one. How you can help: Write a letter to someone in hospital or a care home who may not get much post. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Determined Volunteer Rescues Lost Toddler in the Desert: ‘She may not be our child, but she could be’
item.description: A volunteer grandfather found a toddler lost in the Arizona desert at night and brought her home safe. How you can help: Join a local search-and-rescue or community emergency volunteer team. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: One-of-a-Kind Refuge to 200,000 Walrus Protected Forever in Alaska
item.description: A Bering Sea coastline that shelters up to 200,000 Pacific walrus is now protected for good. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: The City That Kicked Out Cars Before It Was Cool
item.description: Pontevedra in Spain cleared cars from its centre decades ago, and its streets are now safer and busier. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Walk or cycle one short trip a week that you would usually drive. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: This tiny spider named after Stephen Colbert has a genome 50% larger than a human’s
item.description: A tiny California trapdoor spider turns out to carry a genome half again as large as ours. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: New Method Treats Severe Thumb Arthritis With Joint Replacement – Just like a New Hip or Shoulder
item.description: A new thumb joint replacement is restoring grip and hand use for people with severe arthritis. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: ‘Extraordinary’ Drug May Actually Cure High Blood Pressure Caused by Hormones, And it’s FDA-Approved
item.description: An already approved drug may cure high blood pressure caused by a hormone problem, not just control it. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Ask your doctor whether your high blood pressure has been checked for a hormone cause. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Breath of a Whale Captured by Drone Allows Full Genome Sequencing Without Intrusion
item.description: Researchers sequenced a whale's full genome from its breath, caught by drone without touching the animal. Evidence: Early research. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: After 8 years in space, a groundbreaking X-ray telescope finally opens its eyes
item.description: An X-ray telescope bound for Mercury switched on after eight years and works better than expected. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 is now so far away that light takes 24 hours to reach it
item.description: Nearly 50 years after launch, Voyager 1 is still sending signals home from a full light-day away. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: CERN scientists finally find evidence of a particle decay so rare it took 40 years to detect
item.description: After 40 years of searching, CERN found evidence of a particle decay seen once in ten billion events. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Montreal Is Harnessing Soothing Ocean Sounds to Combat Traffic Noise
item.description: A Montreal pocket park plays ocean sounds to soften traffic noise for people resting there. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: CAR-T therapy helps stiff person syndrome patients walk and work again
item.description: A cell therapy helped people with stiff person syndrome walk and return to work in an early Mayo Clinic trial. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
item.description: Five centuries-old baobabs dug up for export were stopped and are being replanted in South Africa. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: Something strange is living beneath the skin of deep-sea pigs
item.description: Scientists found a tiny-genome bacterium living in partnership under the skin of deep-sea sea pigs. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Why hydrogen flames can glow orange, then turn nearly invisible
item.description: Learning why hydrogen flames turn invisible could make future hydrogen stoves safer to use. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: The Waterless, Hyper-Efficient Machines That Clean Clothes With Carbon Dioxide
item.description: New machines clean clothes with recycled carbon dioxide instead of water and harsh solvents. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Can Barbershops Turn Trust Into Better Health for Black Men?
item.description: Staten Island barbershops are using customers' trust to bring health checks to Black men. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Encourage a friend to get their blood pressure checked this month. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Maui Is Becoming a Living Laboratory for Regenerative Tourism
item.description: After the 2023 fires, Maui is inviting visitors to help restore land rather than just pass through. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: When you travel, spend a day volunteering with a local restoration project. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: In Alaska’s capital, food comes by water, air or, most often, community sharing
item.description: In Juneau, with little farmland, residents keep each other fed through traditions of sharing food. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Share surplus from your garden or kitchen with neighbours. Source: The Guardian Environment.
